title: Firmus faces forced share buyback if it can’t resurrect IPO plans
source_used: Australian Financial Review (AFR); only the two opening paragraphs were readable (subscription page)
key_facts: AFR reports that Firmus Technologies could be forced to buy back shares from Nvidia and Blackstone if it fails to resurrect a public listing, under a set of confidential agreements.
AFR says the agreements put the AI infrastructure company on a collision course with the very investors it relies on for financing.

The same agreements suggest that a select group of shareholders, including Nvidia (the microchip maker) and Blackstone (the asset manager), will be in line for free securities if the company does not manage a 25 per cent return on investment guaranteed within three months of the failed float.

Background from our editions: Reuters reported (9 Oct 2026 edition) that Firmus shelved its $5 billion IPO on 9 Oct 2026 after lukewarm demand and would seek private funding; Bloomberg (10 Oct 2026 edition) reported it had sought a $30 billion valuation on $51 million of revenue.
quote_evidence: Firmus Technologies could be forced to buy back shares from Nvidia and Blackstone if it fails to resurrect a public listing under a set of confidential agreements which put the artificial intelligence infrastructure play on a collision course with the very investors it is relying on for financing.

The same agreements suggest that a select group of shareholders including the microchip manufacturer and asset management giant will be in line for free securities if the company does not manage a 25 per cent return on investment guaranteed within three months of the failed float.
why_it_matters_hint: Terms that were kept private show how two of Firmus's biggest backers protected themselves, and how the shelved listing could now cost the company.
event_date: AFR article dated 12 Oct 2026 (listed 11 Oct 2026 23:11 UTC); the agreements are not dated in the part read.
notes: Only the two opening paragraphs (about 650 characters) were readable; the rest is behind AFR's paywall, so the full terms, who the shareholders are beyond Nvidia and Blackstone, and whether any clause has been triggered are not known. No other outlet carries the story (Google News searches). The wording stays inside the opening paragraphs; 'failed float' and 'resurrect' are AFR's words. Follow-up of the 9 Oct 2026 edition (item 10, Reuters, the shelved IPO) and the 10 Oct 2026 edition (item 10, Bloomberg via the Taipei Times, the $30 billion valuation on $51 million of revenue).
